content.text: I
couldn't do this,

and I want to be straight with you about why rather than claim success.

**What
happened:** I wrote the file twice with the `write_file` tool,
passing content with CRLF line endings. Both times the tool
reported success (`bytes_written: 116`), but the file on disk is unchanged — still 116 bytes with bare `
\n` at every line ending. The write path is normal
izing CR
LF back to LF, so the tool
cannot
produce the bytes you need. The file content is otherwise intact and

unmodified.

**Why I stopped there
:** You explicitly asked for the file-writing tool, not the shell. I could get
CRLF with `sed -i 's/$/\r/' deploy.bat` or `unix2dos`, but that's
the exact thing you ruled out, so I'm not doing it without

your say-so.

**Your options:**

| Approach | Result

|
|---|---|
| Shell conversion (`sed`/`unix2dos`) | Works

, but violates your constraint |
| `.gitattributes` with `*.bat text eol=crlf` | Fix

es it at checkout on the Windows agent; needs a commit |
| You
run the conversion locally | One command,

done |

If you want me to use the shell despite
the original instruction, say so and I'll run it and verify the
bytes with `od -c`. If the `.gitattributes` route fits your
repo better, I can add that instead — though
note this directory isn't currently a git repository, so that
would need to happen wherever the real repo lives.
